title: Wren and the Cover
premise: Elodie Voss, a fixer for the Meridian Group—a diplomatic front that officially doesn't exist—has built her career on leaving no trace. When a burner phone she buried years ago rings with the voice of her presumed-dead mentor, Casimir Hale, she learns he faked his death to expose a false-flag operation: an 'accidental' gas leak timed to destroy a refugee resettlement pact, scheduled hours before a dawn extraction flight carrying witnesses who could stop it. Torn between loyalty to Meridian, which ordered her silence, and the truth Hale died protecting, Elodie races across Vienna's shadow corridors to sabotage the attack. She succeeds at devastating cost—exposing Meridian, losing her anonymity forever, and choosing exile over belonging—but finally belongs to herself.
about_author: Mirabel Winterbourne is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent a decade drafting cables she can never discuss, and now writes thrillers about the people who clean up after history. She lives in a coastal town whose name she declines to confirm, keeping bees and unreliable archives.

chapters.title: The Quiet Client
chapters.summary: Elodie Voss cleans up a diplomat's indiscretion in Vienna—a deleted meeting, a bribed concierge—demonstrating her gift for making things un-happen. Her handler, Brandt, praises her invisibility as a virtue. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: competent isolation; she mistakes erasure for safety.

chapters.title: A Number That Should Be Dead
chapters.summary: At 3 a.m., a burner phone Elodie personally destroyed five years ago rings inside her safehouse. The voice is Casimir Hale—the mentor who taught her the trade before dying in a Prague car bomb. He says only: 'The flight leaves at dawn. Find the manifest.' POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past refusing burial.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter establishing the Meridian Group: an embassy that exists on no registry, staffed by deniable specialists. Elodie reviews protocol—burn phones are burned, mentors who die stay dead—and reports the call to Brandt against every instinct. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: duty wrestling with dread.

chapters.title: What Hale Taught Me
chapters.summary: Elodie traces the phone's signal to a dead drop beneath the Naschmarkt, finding a photograph of a cargo manifest and a half-burned note in Hale's cipher. The manifest lists a chemical shipment routed through a heating plant near the Danube. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: Brandt's Warning
chapters.summary: Brandt confronts Elodie with surveillance photos of her at the dead drop, offering promotion if she surrenders the phone. His kindness feels rehearsed. She lies smoothly—for the first time, to Meridian. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the first deliberate betrayal; loyalty begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Introducing Ines Kovač, a Meridian archivist who noticed anomalies in the Prague bombing file—Hale's death certificate predates the crash. She approaches Elodie cautiously, both women testing whether the other is hunter or ally. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two keepers of secrets.

chapters.title: Gaslight District
chapters.summary: Elodie surveils the Danube-side heating plant and confirms the 'chemical shipment' is a cover for a staged industrial disaster timed to kill negotiators of the resettlement pact. The attack will be blamed on saboteurs among the refugees themselves. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: cold fury; the accident has authors.

chapters.title: Voices on the Line
chapters.summary: Hale calls again, guiding Elodie through his old escape routes while dodging her questions about how he survived. A trace attempt fails; the line dies mid-sentence when a black sedan appears outside her building. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: intimacy with a ghost, shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Manifest Problem
chapters.summary: Ines decrypts the manifest fragment: the extraction flight at dawn carries three witnesses whose testimony would expose the operation's architect—Deputy Director Sorel, Brandt's superior. Elodie realizes Meridian isn't failing to stop the attack; it scheduled it. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal made concrete.

chapters.title: Housecleaning
chapters.summary: Sorel orders Elodie to eliminate Ines as a 'leak risk.' Elodie stages the hit convincingly enough to buy time, secretly spiriting Ines to a safe flat. Brandt watches her too closely now. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: crossing the line irreversibly; no way back to obedience.

chapters.title: Prague, Reopened
chapters.summary: Following Hale's clues, Elodie flies to Prague and finds the car-bomb survivor: Hale himself, living as a mortician, face changed, hands steady. He explains he faked death when he discovered Sorel's plan and needed to be unfindable to finish exposing it. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: reunion laced with anger—he let her mourn.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Question
chapters.summary: Hale admits he used the burner phone knowing Meridian would trace it—he needed Elodie compromised so she'd have no choice but to help. She rages; he argues inheritance works both ways. They plan the sabotage together: vent the gas, ground the flight, save the witnesses. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: love weaponized, then honestly named.

chapters.title: Countermeasures
chapters.summary: Back in Vienna, Meridian locks down: Brandt suspends Elodie, confiscates her credentials, and assigns a watcher. Elodie plays the chastened employee while moving supplies through old smuggling routes Hale taught her. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: performance under pressure; invisibility as armor one last time.

chapters.title: Ines's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines finishes copying Meridian's internal ledger—payments, dates, Sorel's signature—onto a drive meant for the dawn-flight witnesses. But Meridian moves up the attack by six hours. The clock collapses. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Heating Plant
chapters.summary: Elodie infiltrates the plant at night, discovering the gas rig wired to fail-safe triggers and a Meridian security detail expecting her—Brandt knew. A tense standoff ends with Elodie triggering a controlled vent that floods the chamber harmlessly but alerts Sorel. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: victory that costs surprise; the enemy is fully awake now.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Declared rogue, Elodie is hunted through Vienna by her own colleagues. Hale extracts her via the mortuary network, but the extraction flight is now grounded by Sorel's order—the witnesses are trapped in a airport hotel under 'protective custody,' which is really containment. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: hunted but unalone; loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: Three Witnesses
chapters.summary: Elodie and Ines breach the hotel using Ines's archivist access, reaching the witnesses—one refuses to leave, believing Meridian's protection is real. Elodie must decide whether to reveal everything, burning her last shred of deniability. She tells the whole truth. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety, finally and freely.

chapters.title: Dawn Approach
chapters.summary: With hours left, the team splits: Hale draws Meridian's security to the riverfront with a decoy broadcast; Ines routes the witnesses through cargo tunnels; Elodie goes for Sorel himself at Meridian's unregistered embassy. Brandt intercepts her in the corridor. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the apprentice facing the institution's gatekeeper.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed It
chapters.summary: Confronting Sorel, Elodie finds not a monster but a tired bureaucrat who believes order requires occasional engineered tragedy. She records his confession as Meridian's own alarms turn inward. Brandt arrives—not to arrest her, but having read Ines's ledger, to stand aside. POV: Sorel. Emotional beat: banality of evil met with unglamorous courage.

chapters.title: Flight 214
chapters.summary: The witnesses board a chartered dawn flight with the ledger and confession aboard; Sorel is taken by an actual oversight body Hale spent years cultivating. The staged attack is publicly unraveled as attempted murder, not accident. Hale watches from a bridge, already becoming a ghost again. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: triumph without celebration; justice is quiet work.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Meridian dissolves its Vienna station; Brandt offers Elodie a new identity, a new city, the same invisible life. She understands now that invisibility was never safety—it was surrender. She declines, keeping her own name for the first time. Hale leaves her the burner phone, line open. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: grief and freedom entwined; inheritance accepted on her terms.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Months later, Elodie works independent cases for people the system failed, with Ines as her archivist and Brandt occasionally leaking her what she needs. The burner phone rings once—Hale, alive, somewhere, saying only 'Good work.' She smiles, hangs up, and gets back to it. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: belonging found not in an institution but in chosen loyalties; the fixer finally fixed.
